the תנא at 62b.9: a fence within a fence, a cave within a cave

props.gloss_en: David to Saul: 'and he said to kill you, and you spared you' (I Sam 24:10)
David to Saul: by Torah law you are liable to be killed
and the Torah said: one who comes to kill you, rise early to kill him
but the modesty that was in you -- it spared you
and what is it? as it is written: 'and he came to the sheepfolds by the way, where there was a cave, and Saul went in to cover his feet' (I Sam 24:4)
a fence within a fence, and a cave within a cave, [where he went in] to cover [his feet]
R' Elazar: [להסך] teaches that he screened himself like a sukka

supports.gloss_en: שהרי רודף אתה, והתורה אמרה: בא להרגך השכם להרגו
ומאי היא? דכתיב: ויבא שאול להסך את רגליו -- the modesty is what this verse describes

objections.gloss_en: "ואמר" -- "ואמרתי" מיבעי ליה! "ותחס" -- "וחסתי" מיבעי ליה! -- David is speaking of himself, so the verse should say 'and I said' and 'and I spared'

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר לו דוד לשאול: מן התורה בן הריגה אתה... והתורה אמרה בא להרגך השכם להרגו, אלא צניעות שהיתה בך היא חסה עליך -- the verbs are not David's: the Torah said [to kill you], and the modesty spared you (= p_shaul_ben_harigah, p_tzniut_chasa; the subject-mapping is carried by the parallel wording, not stated)
